::: {#exr-constant-prediction-decompose}

#### Predicting with one number

A city must predict the crime [rate](#def-event-rate) $Y$ of a randomly chosen neighborhood,
using no [input](#def-input) at all:
it predicts the same number $c$ for every neighborhood.
Let $\mean$ be the [mean](expectation.qmd#def-expectation) $\E{Y}$ of $Y$.
The [expected squared error](expectation.qmd#def-squared-error-risk) of $c$ says how far that one number misses on average,
so it is the quantity the city wants to make small.

Express the expected squared error of the [prediction](expectation.qmd#def-prediction) $c$
as a function of $c$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Apply the [squared error loss](expectation.qmd#def-squared-error-loss) to the number $c$,
and take its [expectation](expectation.qmd#def-expectation).
:::
